newsitem.title: USA: Hilton Hotels debt deal increased in size.
newsitem.headline: Hilton Hotels debt deal increased in size.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp's coming 10-year debt offering was raised in size to $375 million, to meet investor demand for the issue, dealers said on Thursday.
The deal was initially slated at $300 million.
"The offering was upped in size by $75 million," said one dealer. "Unofficial price talk is seen at 105-110 basis points over (Treasuries)."
Hilton's issue carries a coupon reset provision. The provision was embedded to ease the credit risk from its outstanding hostile bid for ITT Corp.
The provision ensures a minimum bump up of 175 basis points in yield should the assumption and/or use of debt prompt a downgrade to junk bond status within three years.
However, analysts said, the provision is likely to go unused as such a downgrade would be extremely unlikely given Hilton's deep committment to investment grade ratings.
Merrill Lynch & Co is expected to serve as lead underwriter for the offering.
